text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouc for their accuracy.

-Guarantees to be given by the government to the religious audiovisual media. A governmental project to deal with the issue of the media workers who lost their jobs includes giving them financial aid for one year and help in finding new jobs.
-Greenpeace ship banned from entering Lebanon. Greenpeace representative Hamdan says the aim of the visit is to show environmental technology.
-Minister of Environment Pharaon says the environmental group wants toeveals the involvement of military personnel and civilians.
-Will the government succeed in ending the tension by establishing a fund for the media workers and returning to dialogue with the General Labour Confederation?
-The government orders security forces to confront the planned protest sit-in of the media workers tomorrow in front of the prime minister's office in Beirut.
-Maronite patriarch Sfeir says supressing press freedom is the start of supressing all freedoms in Lebanon.
-Most of the 49 new deputies in parliament are businessmen
